comment: Resorts of the SnowBuddy ski map data, one per published ski file (written by scripts/export-public-data.mjs in the SnowBuddy repository). Boxes are W, S, E, N in degrees (WGS84): the resort's lifts and runs with at least 2 km to spare on every side, and the out-of-bounds runs in out_of_bounds_named whole at every zoom. osm_timestamp is the OpenStreetMap data the file was built from, and built_at when it was built; pipeline/build-ski.sh rebuilds from it and compares the result with ski_file.sha256. derived_from, where present, names the earlier version whose ski file this is, byte for byte: it rebuilds with the scripts of the commit that published that version.

neighbours.name: Three Summits
neighbours.reason: OpenStreetMap's polygon of Summit West, Central and East, The Summit at Snoqualmie's other three areas across Interstate 90 (Summit West's own polygon, way/1499174311, lies inside it): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), joined to Alpental by no lift or trail (summitatsnoqualmie.com/summit-shuttle, the free bus between the Summit areas and Alpental, whose crossover trails join only Summit West, Central and East; Alpental's trail map, summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps: 'Shuttle or drive to Summit West, Central, East'). Summit West lies in the south-east of the box, the rest in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Sahalie Ski Club
neighbours.reason: A private ski club (access=private, its rope tow tagged 'Private Club Lift') 0.4 km north of Summit West's polygon and 1.6 km south-east of Alpental's base, on the road between them: not on The Summit at Snoqualmie's ticket, maps or lift report, and its polygon holds the club's rope tow, which would otherwise draw as a lift in the box. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Snowbird
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, west down Little Cottonwood Canyon and sharing Alta's west border along the Baldy shoulder and Sugarloaf Pass (the Alta-Snowbird connection): its polygon lies almost whole in the box, with its 14 lifts and some 230 runs and run areas. A run along the shared border stays with the resort that holds most of it (the Sugarloaf Connector, 62% in Snowbird's polygon, goes with Snowbird; the Shoulder Traverse and Baldy Chutes, 92% and more in Alta's, stay).

neighbours.name: Brighton Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon over the ridge north-east of Albion Basin: its polygon reaches into the box's east side, with its lifts and runs in the Overpass window.

neighbours.name: Solitude Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon north of Alta, over the Grizzly Gulch and Twin Lakes ridges: its polygon lies inside the box's north-east, with its lifts and runs in the Overpass window.

neighbours.name: Park City Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort over the Wasatch crest to the north-east: its Jupiter side (11 lifts and some 130 runs in the Overpass window, as at Brighton) reaches the window's east, outside the box, and would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Loveland Basin Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Loveland Ski Area's main side, a separate resort on its own ticket across Loveland Pass, 1.8 km north of Arapahoe Basin's polygon: its polygon reaches into the box's north edge, with its lifts and runs (Chet's Dream, Lifts 2, 4, 6, 8 and 9 and the Ptarmigan Lift) in the box and the Overpass margin. Over the Rainbow, 91% inside it, goes with it; the Porcupine Ridge Bootpack along the shared ridge is a hike-tagged way the pipeline leaves out anyway.

neighbours.name: Loveland Valley Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Loveland's beginner side, east of US 6 below the pass: its polygon, Lifts 3 and 7 and two carpets lie in the Overpass margin north of the box and would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Keystone
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket to the west: its polygon's east side (the Outback and the Montezuma Express, with the River Run Gondola, the Summit and Peru Express and the Discovery area in the Overpass margin) reaches into the box's west edge, 1 km west of Arapahoe Basin's polygon, so its lifts and runs would otherwise draw beside A-Basin's.

neighbours.name: Aspen Mountain
neighbours.reason: Aspen Mountain, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 1.6 km east across Castle Creek above the town of Aspen, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Aspen Highlands by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; aspen-mountain). Half of its polygon lies in the box's east part, the rest in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Buttermilk
neighbours.reason: Buttermilk, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 0.6 km north across Maroon Creek, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Aspen Highlands by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; buttermilk). Its polygon lies wholly in the box's north part, with its lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Aspen Snowmass
neighbours.reason: Snowmass (its polygon named Aspen Snowmass in OpenStreetMap), another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 4.1 km north-west above Snowmass Village, with its own bases, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Aspen Highlands by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; snowmass). Half of its polygon (Elk Camp and Two Creeks) lies in the Overpass window west of the box, with those lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Aspen Highlands
neighbours.reason: Aspen Highlands, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 1.6 km west across Castle Creek, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Aspen Mountain by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page, the free shuttle to all mountains from Rubey Park on Aspen Mountain's 2025-26 map): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; aspen-highlands). Its polygon reaches into the box's west part, with its lifts and runs in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Buttermilk
neighbours.reason: Buttermilk, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 2.3 km north-west beyond Castle Creek and Maroon Creek, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Aspen Mountain by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; buttermilk). Its polygon reaches into the box's north-west corner, with its lifts and runs in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Bear Notch Ski Touring Center
neighbours.reason: The Bear Notch Ski Touring Center's cross-country centre, a separate venue with its own passes on Bear Notch Road 1.6 km west of Bear Peak: its polygon (the centre's nordic trails) reaches into the box's west edge, so it is listed by the neighbour rule; it holds no lift or downhill run of the resort's, and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule anyway.

neighbours.name: Snow Summit
neighbours.reason: Snow Summit, the resort's other mountain, on its own map (snow-summit; the combined map, big-bear-mountain-resort, retired on 2026-11-15 by the owner's rule of one map per ski area unless connected by lift or trail): its polygon lies inside the box's west half, 2 km west of Bear Mountain, with its 15 lifts and 40 runs.

neighbours.name: Big Bear Snow Play
neighbours.reason: a separate snow play area (sledding and tubing) with its two carpets, not part of the ski resort; in the Overpass margin north of the box, where the two carpets would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles

neighbours.name: Bear Valley Adventure Company
neighbours.reason: Bear Valley's cross-country centre by the village and Highway 4 (Bear Valley Adventure Company, its own trails and tickets; OpenStreetMap's site relation/7025848): its polygon reaches from the box's south edge to 0.4 km from the ski area's, with the nordic trails the type rule leaves out. Left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21, so the map draws only the downhill resort.

neighbours.name: Snow Play Area
neighbours.reason: The Bear Valley Adventure Company's snow play area at the village, 0.6 km south of the ski area's polygon inside the box: a separate venue (sledding and tubing), not part of the ski resort.

neighbours.name: Sledding area
neighbours.reason: The Bear Valley Adventure Company's sledding hill beside its snow play area at the village, 0.7 km south of the ski area's polygon inside the box: a separate venue, not part of the ski resort; its sled lines are left out by the type rule.

neighbours.name: Yellowstone Club
neighbours.reason: A private club, not on Big Sky's ticket, south of Andesite Mountain and Lone Mountain's south face: its polygon (Pioneer Mountain, the Eglise Gondola and its chairs) fills the box's south half and shares a border with Big Sky's (73 nodes), so its 21 lifts and 121 runs would otherwise draw beside Big Sky's. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Jackson Creek Summit
neighbours.reason: Jackson Creek Summit (formerly Indianhead), Snowriver Mountain Resort's main mountain, about 600 m east, across Blackjack Road, with its own chalet, six lifts and trail network, joined to Black River Basin by no lift or ski trail, only the resort's base-to-base shuttle (snowriver.com/mountain-info/trail-map-mountain-stats: "two mountains—Jackson Creek Summit and Black River Basin, which are separated by a brief shuttle ride"; mountain-info/hours-of-operation: the Base-to-Base Shuttle between the base of the Voyageur Express and the Black River Chalet; read 2026-11-14): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14). Its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies whole in the east of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Craigleith Ski Club
neighbours.reason: A private members' ski club on the Niagara Escarpment, not on Blue Mountain's ticket or trail map: its polygon adjoins Blue Mountain's north side inside the box, so its lifts (Funnel, Comet, National, V-Hill, Little John and the Zipper carpet) and runs would otherwise draw as Blue Mountain's. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off"): the neighbouring private clubs are never drawn as Blue Mountain's.

neighbours.name: Alpine Ski Club
neighbours.reason: A private members' ski club on the Niagara Escarpment north of Craigleith, not on Blue Mountain's ticket or trail map: its polygon lies inside the box's north-west corner, so its lifts (Summit Express, the Arrowhead, Millennium and Steeps chairs and the Square One carpet) and runs would otherwise draw beside Blue Mountain's. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off"): the neighbouring private clubs are never drawn as Blue Mountain's.

neighbours.name: Osler Bluff Ski Club
neighbours.reason: A private members' ski club on the Niagara Escarpment 2.5 km south of Blue Mountain, not on its ticket or trail map: its polygon reaches into the box's south edge, so its lifts (the Poplar, Clubhouse and Exhibition chairs and the Beehive J-bar) and runs would otherwise draw at the box's south edge. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off"): the neighbouring private clubs are never drawn as Blue Mountain's.

neighbours.name: Georgian Peaks Club
neighbours.reason: A private members' ski club on the Niagara Escarpment north-west of Alpine, not on Blue Mountain's ticket or trail map: its polygon ends about 175 m west of the box, in the Overpass margin, so its lifts (Champlain Express, Roger's Chair, Minute Mile Chair, Bay Street Chair and the Riot Platter) and runs would otherwise draw at the box's north-west corner. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off"): the neighbouring private clubs are never drawn as Blue Mountain's.

neighbours.name: Sugar Bowl Resort
neighbours.reason: Sugar Bowl, a separate resort on its own ticket south of Donner Pass Road: its polygon's north part (the Village Gondola and Mt. Judah) lies in the box's south-east corner and the rest (Mt. Disney and Mt. Lincoln) in the Overpass window, 1.1 km from Boreal's nearest run, with no lift or trail between them.

neighbours.name: Brandywine Ski Resort
neighbours.reason: Brandywine, the other hill on Boston Mills' Epic card (bmbw.com, Boston Mills Brandywine), about 2 km north-east in the Cuyahoga Valley with its own lodge, lifts and trail map and joined to Boston Mills by no lift or trail (one map each, the owner's rule of 2026-11-14): its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies in the north-east of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Boston Mills Ski Resort
neighbours.reason: Boston Mills, the other hill on Brandywine's Epic card (bmbw.com, Boston Mills Brandywine), about 2 km south-west in the Cuyahoga Valley with its own lodge, lifts and trail map and joined to Brandywine by no lift or trail (one map each, the owner's rule of 2026-11-14): its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies in the south-west of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Copper Mountain
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, west over the Tenmile Range: its polygon's east side (Copper Bowl, Union Peak) reaches the Overpass window west of the box, and the bottom of its Alpine lift lies just inside the box's west edge, where its lifts and runs would otherwise draw beside Breckenridge's Peak 6 and Peak 7.

neighbours.name: Solitude Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, west across the Silver Fork ridge: 6 lifts and 74 runs and run areas in the box, more in the margin. Solbright, the run from Solitude down to Brighton's base, lies 87% inside it and goes with it (owner's rule, accepted).

neighbours.name: Alta Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon: its east side reaches into the box (4 lifts, 73 runs and run areas), the rest lies in the margin.

neighbours.name: Snowbird
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Overpass margin (12 lifts, 230 runs and run areas).

neighbours.name: Park City Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort over the Wasatch crest to the east: its Jupiter side reaches into the box (1 lift, 39 runs), more in the margin.

neighbours.name: Deer Valley Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort: its Empire side lies in the Overpass margin (11 lifts, 121 runs and run areas).

neighbours.name: Aspen Highlands
neighbours.reason: Aspen Highlands, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 0.6 km south across Maroon Creek, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Buttermilk by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; aspen-highlands). A third of its polygon (its lower mountain down to the Highlands base) lies in the box's south part, the rest in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Aspen Mountain
neighbours.reason: Aspen Mountain, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 2.3 km south-east above the town of Aspen, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Buttermilk by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; aspen-mountain). Its polygon's west tip lies at the box's east edge, the rest in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Aspen Snowmass
neighbours.reason: Snowmass (its polygon named Aspen Snowmass in OpenStreetMap), another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 2.4 km west above Snowmass Village, with its own bases, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Buttermilk by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; snowmass). Half of its polygon (Elk Camp and Two Creeks) lies in the Overpass window west of the box, with those lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Breckenridge
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket over the Tenmile Range to the east: its polygon's west edge (the Peak 7 and Peak 8 side) reaches about 400 m into the box's east edge, 2 km from Copper's polygon, and more of it lies in the Overpass margin, where its lifts and runs (the BreckConnect Gondola, 6-Chair, the Peak 7 and Peak 8 lifts) would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles. The Cimarron Start House, a 9 m landuse=winter_sports way inside Breckenridge's polygon (way/470098262), has no lifts or runs of its own and is not listed.

neighbours.name: Crested Butte Nordic
neighbours.reason: The town's nordic centre, a separate venue with its own passes: its multipolygon (two outer rings, the trails around the town of Crested Butte and below Mount Crested Butte's south-west side) touches no part of the resort's polygon and holds no lift or downhill run, but reaches into the box's west half, so it is listed by the neighbour rule; nothing of the resort is left off by it (normalize.json: no lift, run, run area or station), and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule anyway.

neighbours.name: Park City Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort and ticket with no interconnect: its Park City side, Jupiter to the Town Lift, lies in the box (19 lifts, 262 runs), more in the margin.

neighbours.name: Brighton Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, in the Overpass margin (8 lifts, 89 runs).

neighbours.name: Solitude Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, in the Overpass margin (6 lifts, 30 runs).

neighbours.name: Sun Valley - Bald Mountain
neighbours.reason: Bald Mountain, a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14): sun-valley. Its polygon lies 1.8 km west of Dollar Mountain's across the Big Wood River, joined to it by no lift or ski trail (sunvalley.com/the-mountain/maps-guides gives each mountain its own 2026-27 trail map, and sunvalley.com/about/getting-here sends guests between the two on the free Mountain Rides bus), and reaches into the box's west edge with the River Run base and its lifts and runs.

neighbours.name: Sugar Bowl Resort
neighbours.reason: Sugar Bowl, a separate resort on its own ticket across Donner Pass Road: most of its polygon (the Village Gondola, Mt. Judah, Jerome Hill and Mt. Disney) lies in the box's south half and the rest (Mt. Lincoln) in the Overpass window, 250 m from Donner Ski Ranch's lowest run, and no lift or trail joins the two (Donner Ski Ranch's map ends at Donner Pass Road).

neighbours.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Tahoe Donner, a separate resort above Donner Lake 6 km north-east of Donner Ski Ranch: its polygon's west edge and its lifts and runs lie in the Overpass window's north-east corner, outside the box, where they would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Island Lake Cat Skiing
neighbours.reason: Island Lake Lodge's cat-skiing tenure (access=private), a separate operation not on Fernie's ticket, on the Lizard Range north-west of the resort: its polygon reaches into the box's north-west corner, and its freeride lines, all inside it and tagged backcountry, would otherwise draw as out-of-bounds runs on Fernie's map.

neighbours.name: Seven Springs Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, 5 km south-west on the same ridge: its polygon reaches the Overpass window south-west of the box, with its North Face and front-side lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Black River Basin
neighbours.reason: Black River Basin (formerly Blackjack), Snowriver Mountain Resort's other mountain, about 600 m west, across Blackjack Road, with its own chalet, four chairs and trail network, joined to Jackson Creek Summit by no lift or ski trail, only the resort's base-to-base shuttle (snowriver.com/mountain-info/trail-map-mountain-stats: "two mountains—Jackson Creek Summit and Black River Basin, which are separated by a brief shuttle ride"; mountain-info/hours-of-operation: the Base-to-Base Shuttle between the base of the Voyageur Express and the Black River Chalet; read 2026-11-14): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14). Its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies whole in the west of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Arapahoe Basin
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, 3 km east of Keystone's polygon up Highway 6: its polygon's west side (the Beavers and Zuma lifts, Montezuma Bowl) reaches into the box's east edge, the rest lies in the Overpass margin, where its lifts and runs would otherwise draw beside The Outback and Bergman Bowl.

neighbours.name: Pico Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Pico Mountain, a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14): pico. Its polygon lies 1.8 km north-west of Killington's, joined to it by no lift or ski trail (each has its own 2026-27 trail map and lift list; the Killington/Pico Interconnect on killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status is an uphill travel route, and picomountain.com/transportation-parking-and-shuttles sends guests on to Killington by The Bus), and reaches into the box's north-west corner with its lifts and runs.

neighbours.name: Fox Hill Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Fox Hill, the Milwaukee Ski Club's private members' hill (OpenStreetMap's operator tag; skiresort.info names the club as its lift operator) on County Highway NN, about 4 km north-east of Little Switzerland's boundary, with its own four rope tows and runs and no lift, trail or ticket shared with Little Switzerland: a separate ski area. Its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies north of the box in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Kanc Recreation Area
neighbours.reason: A separate venue in Lincoln, west of Loon's West Basin and inside the box: a small hill with its own rope tow (Kanc Rope Tow), four named runs (Papoose, Brave, Chief and Kanc Park) and five short unnamed ones, on no Loon trail map or lift list (the resort counts 13 lifts, none of them a rope tow). Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: The Hermitage Club at Haystack Mountain
neighbours.reason: A private members' club on Haystack Mountain (its Barnstormer chair's station is tagged 'Private Ski Area Chair Lift', operator The Hermitage Club), not on Mount Snow's ticket or trail map, 2.3 km south of Mount Snow's polygon: its polygon ends 85 m south of the box, in the Overpass margin, so its lifts and runs would otherwise draw at the box's south edge. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Palisades Tahoe Olympic Valley
neighbours.reason: Palisades Tahoe, a separate resort 7 km south-west of Northstar's polygon: its Olympic Valley side (the village, the Aerial Tram, KT-22, Red Dog, the Far East Express and their runs, 15 lifts in all) reaches the Overpass window west of the box, where its lifts would draw at the pack's edge at z10 as Northstar's Backside Express did on Palisades' map.

neighbours.name: Northstar at Tahoe Resort
neighbours.reason: Northstar California, a separate resort 7 km north-east of Palisades' polygons: its south-side lifts and runs (Backside Express, Monument glade and others) reach the Overpass window, and Backside Express would draw as a lift line at z10.

neighbours.name: Homewood Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Homewood, a separate resort on Lake Tahoe's west shore south of Alpine Meadows: the box widened for the trail-map view (2026-10-23) brings its lifts and runs into the Overpass window.

neighbours.name: Homewood Snowcat Adventures
neighbours.reason: Homewood's snowcat skiing area, not Palisades' terrain, in the widened window (2026-10-23).

neighbours.name: Deer Valley Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort and ticket with no interconnect, beside the Park City side: 23 lifts and 246 runs and run areas in the box. Its Snow Park stragglers just outside its polygon (American Flag, way/1488981500, the platter way/1210150101) go with it by the 250 m pass.

neighbours.name: Solitude Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, inside the box's south-west corner: 9 lifts, 94 runs and run areas.

neighbours.name: Brighton Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, partly in the box's south-west corner: 6 lifts and 68 runs in the box, 2 lifts and 21 runs in the margin.

neighbours.name: Utah Olympic Park
neighbours.reason: Separate venue (ski jumps, training runs) north of Canyons: 5 lifts and 21 runs in the box.

neighbours.name: Alta Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon: 1 lift and 1 run in the box, the rest in the margin.

neighbours.name: Snowbird
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Overpass margin (8 lifts, 120 runs and run areas).

neighbours.name: Killington Resort
neighbours.reason: Killington, a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14): killington. Its polygon lies 1.8 km south-east of Pico's, joined to it by no lift or ski trail (each has its own 2026-27 trail map and lift list; the Killington/Pico Interconnect on killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status is an uphill travel route, and picomountain.com/transportation-parking-and-shuttles sends guests on to Killington by The Bus), and reaches into the box's south-east corner with Ramshead, Snowdon and the K-1 base and their lifts and runs.

neighbours.name: Hidden Valley Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, 5 km north-east on the same ridge: its polygon's west tip reaches the box's north-east corner and the rest of it, with its lifts and runs, lies in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Snowshoe Mountain
neighbours.reason: Snowshoe Basin with the Western Territory across the road (named Snowshoe Mountain in OpenStreetMap, as Silver Creek's polygon is), Snowshoe Mountain's main areas under the village, 1.4 km south of Silver Creek's polygon across a wooded valley: a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), joined to Silver Creek by no lift or trail (Snowshoe's trail map, the James Niehues painting, draws no run or lift between them, only a wooded valley, and a bus stop at each base; snowshoemtn.com's Silver Creek page offers a 'free shuttle to & from' and its shuttle page runs continuous loops between Silver Creek, the Village and Top of the World (the Internet Archive's copies of 2025-03-13 and 2024-12-12: the site itself answers automated requests with a bot wall)). Its northern part lies in the south of the box, most of the rest in the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Sovereign Lake Nordic Club
neighbours.reason: a separate cross-country ski club 2.4 km west of the resort's polygon, at the box's west edge, with no lift or downhill run of its own (its trails are nordic, which the map leaves out)

neighbours.name: Big Bear Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Bear Mountain, the resort's other mountain, on its own map (bear-mountain; the combined map, big-bear-mountain-resort, retired on 2026-11-15 by the owner's rule of one map per ski area unless connected by lift or trail): its polygon (named Big Bear Mountain Resort in OpenStreetMap) crosses the box's east edge 2 km east of Snow Summit, with its 11 lifts and 26 runs in the Overpass window.

neighbours.name: Big Bear Snow Play
neighbours.reason: a separate snow play area (sledding and tubing) with its two carpets, not part of the ski resort

neighbours.name: Alta Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, east up Little Cottonwood Canyon and sharing Snowbird's east border along the Baldy shoulder and Sugarloaf Pass (the Alta-Snowbird connection): its polygon lies almost whole in the box, with its 11 lifts and some 150 runs and run areas. A run along the shared border stays with the resort that holds most of it (the Sugarloaf Connector, 62% in Snowbird's polygon, stays; Westward Ho and the Shoulder Traverse, wholly or 92% in Alta's, go with Alta).

neighbours.name: Brighton Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, north-east over the Wasatch crest: its polygon's west side reaches the Overpass window's north-east corner, outside the box, with lifts and runs that would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Solitude Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Big Cottonwood Canyon, north over the Twin Lakes ridge: its polygon lies in the Overpass window's north-east, with its lifts and runs, partly inside the box's north-east corner.

neighbours.name: Park City Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort over the Wasatch crest to the north-east: its Jupiter side (11 lifts and some 130 runs, Scott's Bowl and the Jupiter chutes among them) lies in the Overpass window's north-east corner, outside the box; unlisted, its runs there would draw as in-bounds runs of nobody's in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Buttermilk
neighbours.reason: Buttermilk, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 2.4 km east, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Snowmass by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; buttermilk). Its polygon lies wholly in the Overpass window east of the box, with its lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Aspen Highlands
neighbours.reason: Aspen Highlands, another of Aspen Snowmass's four mountains on one ticket, about 4.1 km south-east beyond Buttermilk, with its own base, lifts, ski area boundary and trail map, and joined to Snowmass by no lift or trail (the resort's free buses run between the four mountains: the 4-Mountain Connector on its Getting Around page): a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14; aspen-highlands). Its polygon lies in the Overpass window east of the box, with its lifts and runs; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Snowshoe Mountain
neighbours.reason: Silver Creek (named Snowshoe Mountain in OpenStreetMap, as the Basin's polygon is), Snowshoe Mountain's third area, 1.4 km north of Snowshoe Basin's polygon across a wooded valley: a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), joined to Snowshoe Basin and the Western Territory by no lift or trail (Snowshoe's trail map, the James Niehues painting, draws no run or lift between them, only a wooded valley, and a bus stop at each base; snowshoemtn.com's Silver Creek page offers a 'free shuttle to & from' and its shuttle page runs continuous loops between Silver Creek, the Village and Top of the World (the Internet Archive's copies of 2025-03-13 and 2024-12-12: the site itself answers automated requests with a bot wall)). It lies in the north of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Brighton Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, up the canyon east of Solitude's polygon, inside the box: its lifts and runs would otherwise draw beside Solitude's. The Sol-Bright connection stays with Solitude: Solbright (way/618578232), the run from Solitude's Summit Express top down to Brighton's base, lies 87% inside Solitude's polygon, as Brighton's own map leaves it to Solitude.

neighbours.name: Alta Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon, over the ridge south of Solitude: its polygon reaches into the box's south-west quarter, the rest lies in the Overpass margin.

neighbours.name: Snowbird
neighbours.reason: Separate resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon: its polygon's north-east corner reaches into the box's south-west corner, the rest lies in the Overpass margin.

neighbours.name: Park City Mountain Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort over the Wasatch crest to the east: its Jupiter side reaches into the box's north-east corner, more in the Overpass margin.

neighbours.name: Deer Valley Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort: its Empire side (Daly Bowl, Solace, Buckeye and their chutes) lies in the Overpass margin east of the box and would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles.

neighbours.name: Howelson Hill Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Howelsen Hill (OSM spells it Howelson), the City of Steamboat Springs' own ski area in town, 3 km west of the gondola: another venue with its own tickets. Left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21; its 17 runs and 4 lifts would otherwise draw on Steamboat's map and take trunk ranks in its overview (Long John, Wren's Run).

neighbours.name: Smugglers' Notch Resort
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket, north over Smugglers' Notch (Vermont Route 108, closed to vehicles in winter): its polygon (Sterling, Madonna and Morse Mountains) reaches into the box's north edge 0.5 km north of Stowe's Spruce Peak, so its lifts and runs would otherwise draw beside Stowe's. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Trapp Family Lodge
neighbours.reason: The Trapp Family Lodge's cross-country centre, a separate venue with its own passes: its polygon (the lodge's nordic trails south of the Toll House base) reaches into the box's south edge, so it is listed by the neighbour rule; it holds no lift or downhill run of the resort's, and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule anyway.

neighbours.name: The Nordic Center at Edson Hill
neighbours.reason: The Edson Hill inn's nordic centre, a separate venue (OpenStreetMap maps it as its building, tagged landuse=winter_sports) inside the box's east edge, 2.5 km east of the Toll House base: listed by the neighbour rule; it holds no lift or downhill run of the resort's, and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule anyway.

neighbours.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill Ski Area
neighbours.reason: Tahoe Donner, a separate resort above Donner Lake 7 km north-east of Sugar Bowl's polygon: its polygon, 5 lifts and 23 runs lie in the Overpass window's north-east corner, outside the box, and would otherwise draw in the z10-12 edge tiles. Donner Ski Ranch, Boreal and Soda Springs, which lie inside the box, have no landuse=winter_sports polygon in OpenStreetMap and are hidden by overrides instead (sugar-bowl.overrides.json).

neighbours.name: Mad River Glen
neighbours.reason: Separate resort on its own ticket (a skier-owned cooperative), north of Mount Ellen on General Stark Mountain: its polygon lies 1 km north of Sugarbush's and reaches into the box's north edge, so its lifts (the Single Chair among them) and runs would otherwise draw beside Mount Ellen's. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Maine Huts and Trails
neighbours.reason: Maine Huts and Trails, a separate non-profit's hut-to-hut trail network: its polygon (the network's land from Carrabassett Valley north to the Dead River, about 20 km2) reaches into the box's north edge north of Sugarloaf's Outdoor Center, so it is listed by the neighbour rule; it holds no lift or downhill run of the resort's, and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule anyway.

neighbours.name: Sahalie Ski Club
neighbours.reason: A private ski club (access=private, its rope tow tagged 'Private Club Lift') 0.4 km north of Summit West's polygon, on the way to Alpental: not on The Summit at Snoqualmie's ticket, maps or lift report, and its polygon holds the club's rope tow, which would otherwise draw as a lift between the resort's areas. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off").

neighbours.name: Alpental
neighbours.reason: Alpental, The Summit at Snoqualmie's fourth area, across Interstate 90 from Summit West: a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), joined to Summit West, Central and East by no lift or trail (summitatsnoqualmie.com/summit-shuttle, the free bus between the Summit areas and Alpental, whose crossover trails join only Summit West, Central and East; Alpental's trail map, summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps: 'Shuttle or drive to Summit West, Central, East'). Its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies in the north-west of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Alpental Backcountry
neighbours.reason: OpenStreetMap's polygon of the Alpental Back Bowls, beyond Alpental's Back Bowl Boundary and gates (Alpental's trail map, summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) and reached only from Alpental's lifts: part of Alpental, a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), where its runs are drawn out of bounds. It reaches into the north-west corner of the box and lies in the Overpass window; left off, so that none of its backcountry lines draws on The Summit's map.

neighbours.name: Sun Valley - Dollar Mountain
neighbours.reason: Dollar Mountain, a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14): dollar-mountain. Its polygon lies 1.8 km east of Bald Mountain's across the Big Wood River, joined to it by no lift or ski trail (sunvalley.com/the-mountain/maps-guides gives each mountain its own 2026-27 trail map, and sunvalley.com/about/getting-here sends guests between the two on the free Mountain Rides bus), and reaches into the box's east edge with its lifts and runs.

neighbours.name: Nub's Nob
neighbours.reason: Separate ski area on its own ticket and under its own owner, 1 km east of The Highlands' boundary on the same ridge north of Harbor Springs: its polygon, with its lifts and runs, lies in the east of the box and the Overpass window; left off by the owner's rule of 2026-10-21.

neighbours.name: Tuckerman Ravine
neighbours.reason: Mount Washington's backcountry bowl across Pinkham Notch (Route 16) from Wildcat, reached on foot from the Pinkham Notch Visitor Center: no lift, no patrol and not on Wildcat's ticket or trail map. Its polygon reaches into the box's west edge, so its gullies (Left Gully, The Chute, Lobster Claw, Right Gully, the Lip, the Sluice) would otherwise draw beside Wildcat's runs. Left off by the owner's rule ("leave them off"): Mount Washington's backcountry is not Wildcat's.

neighbours.name: Great Glen Trails
neighbours.reason: Great Glen Trails' nordic and snowshoe centre, a separate venue with its own passes on Route 16 2 km north of Wildcat's base: its polygon reaches into the box's north edge, so it is listed by the neighbour rule; it holds no lift or downhill run of the resort's, and its nordic, snowshoe, hiking and tubing ways are left out by the type rule anyway.
